==Problem==
If <math>a @ b = \frac{a\times b}{a+b}</math> for <math>a,b</math> positive integers, then what is <math>5 @10</math>? 

<math>\textbf{(A)}\ \frac{3}{10} \qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 1 \qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 2 \qquad\textbf{(D)}\ \frac{10}{3} \qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 50</math>

==Solution==
Substitute <math>a=5</math> and <math>b=10</math> into the expression for <math>a @ b</math> to get:

<math>5 @ 10 = \frac{5\times 10}{5+10} = \frac{50}{15} = \frac{10}{3}</math>

Thus, answer choice <math>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ \frac{10}{3}}</math> is correct.
